precepts.text: The angel says the same thing again: I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren the prophets. Worship God.
precepts.point: John fell at the angel's feet to worship him, and he said, See thou do it not: I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren. The angels are our brethren; the angels have tribes too. In Revelation 21, do not be surprised if the angels at the twelve gates stand each at the gate of their tribe.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
John says it twice. In Revelation 19 he fell at the angel's feet, and here again: “I John saw these things, and heard them. And when I had heard and seen, I fell down to worship before the feet of the angel which shewed me these things.”

And the angel says the same thing again: “See thou do it not: for I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren the prophets, and of them which keep the sayings of this book: worship God.” He will not take worship, because he is not God. He is a fellowservant, one of the brethren.

That is who the angels are: our brothers. They are not demons. They ate with Lot because they have mouths just like us, and they were going to lie down because they look like us. Esau calls them humanoids, and to Esau they are going to be some demons, but those are our brothers. The angels have tribes too, and in Revelation 21, do not be surprised if the angels standing at the twelve gates are each standing at the gate of their own tribe.

precepts.text: This is Raphael speaking to Tobit, presenting himself as Azarias of his brethren; and Tobit answers, Thou art welcome, brother, and asks after his tribe and his family: thou art my brother, of an honest and good stock.
precepts.point: John fell at the angel's feet to worship him, and he said, See thou do it not: I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren. The angels are our brethren; the angels have tribes too. In Revelation 21, do not be surprised if the angels at the twelve gates stand each at the gate of their tribe.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
Here Raphael, before he makes himself known, presents himself to Tobit another way: “I am Azarias, the son of Ananias the great, and of thy brethren.” An angel of God naming himself as one of the brethren, just as the angel told John, “I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren.”

Tobit answers, “Thou art welcome, brother; be not now angry with me, because I have enquired to know thy tribe and thy family; for thou art my brother, of an honest and good stock.” Tobit asks after his tribe and his family, and receives him as a brother.

He knows his people: “I know Ananias and Jonathas, sons of that great Samaias, as we went together to Jerusalem to worship, and offered the firstborn, and the tenths of the fruits; and they were not seduced with the error of our brethren: my brother, thou art of a good stock.”

So the angel who walked with Tobit's son was taken for an Israelite brother, of a tribe and a family. That is how close the angels are to us: they look like us, they have tribes too, and they are our brethren.

precepts.text: I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels, which present the prayers of the saints: because they minister unto us; they are ministering spirits working on our behalf, because those are our brothers. They are not demonic spirits sent here to oppose people. That is popular persuasion; that is lies.
precepts.point: John fell at the angel's feet to worship him, and he said, See thou do it not: I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren. The angels are our brethren; the angels have tribes too. In Revelation 21, do not be surprised if the angels at the twelve gates stand each at the gate of their tribe.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
Now Raphael makes himself known: “I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels, which present the prayers of the saints, and which go in and out before the glory of the Holy One.” The one Tobit called brother, Azarias of his brethren, was the angel all along.

Why do the angels present the prayers of the saints? Because they minister unto us. They are ministering spirits working on our behalf, because those are our brothers.

They are not demonic spirits sent here to oppose the people that inhabit this place called the United Snakes of America. That is untrue. That is popular persuasion; that is lies. The world is being taught to call what comes out of the heavens demons and fallen angels, so that it will gather to fight against Christ and his army. But the angels are our brethren, fellowservants who keep the testimony of Jesus, and we worship God alone.

precepts.text: I will take vengeance, and I will not meet thee as a man: Christ is coming back with that immortal body. You will not be able to nail him back to the cross like you did in Jerusalem. That is what the fine linen, white and clean, is making reference to.
precepts.point: And I saw the beast, and the kings of the earth, and their armies, gathered together to make war against him that sat on the horse, and against his army. There it is: gathered together, minds already persuaded. And the beast was taken, and with him the false prophet, and these both were cast alive into a lake of fire burning with brimstone.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
The armies in heaven follow Christ “upon white horses, clothed in fine linen, white and clean.” That fine linen, white and clean, is the immortal body. To prove it, go to Isaiah, speaking to Babylon: “Thy nakedness shall be uncovered, yea, thy shame shall be seen: I will take vengeance, and I will not meet thee as a man.”

Christ said he is going to take vengeance, and he will not meet Babylon as a man. Christ is coming back with that immortal body. You will not be able to nail him back to the cross like you did in Jerusalem.

That is what the white horse and the fine linen, white and clean, make reference to. And he comes to make war, because God is a man of war: “in righteousness he doth judge and make war.” His vesture is dipped in blood, because there is going to be a lot of bloodshed, a lot of killing. On his head are many crowns, because he is going to take everyone's crowns and be the one King, “KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS.”

precepts.text: Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him: that's us, the Israelites, before Esau and the nations that made no account of our labours. When they see it, they shall be troubled with terrible fear, and shall be amazed at the strangeness of his salvation: the chariots, and us being taken up; that is going to be strange and foreign to them. That is going to be the new talk of the town: a black God and a black Christ coming to redeem his people. And they repenting shall say, This was he whom we had sometimes in derision: how is he numbered among the children of God, and his lot is among the saints!
precepts.point: And I saw the beast, and the kings of the earth, and their armies, gathered together to make war against him that sat on the horse, and against his army. There it is: gathered together, minds already persuaded. And the beast was taken, and with him the false prophet, and these both were cast alive into a lake of fire burning with brimstone.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
Revelation says the beast and the kings of the earth and their armies were gathered together to make war against him that sits on the horse. Wisdom shows what happens when they see him: “Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.” That is us, the Israelites, standing before Esau and the nations, who made no account of our labours here.

“When they see it, they shall be troubled with terrible fear, and shall be amazed at the strangeness of his salvation, so far beyond all that they looked for.” The strangeness of his salvation is the chariots, us being taken up. That is going to be strange and foreign to them. They will no longer talk about the deliverance out of Egypt, but about the new deliverance from the land of the north. A black God, a black Christ, coming to redeem his black people: that is going to be the new talk of the town.

“And they repenting and groaning for anguish of spirit shall say within themselves, This was he, whom we had sometimes in derision, and a proverb of reproach.” Christ is going to put it in their mind: these are the people you afflicted, raped, robbed, murdered and enslaved. These are my people.

“We fools accounted his life madness, and his end to be without honour: How is he numbered among the children of God, and his lot is among the saints! Therefore have we erred from the way of truth.”

precepts.text: The man that came out of the sea is Christ: whensoever the voice went out of his mouth, all they burned that heard his voice, because they were guilty of that law. There was gathered together a multitude of men out of number from the four winds of heaven to subdue him: they will have one consent, because the Most High is going to harden them like he did Pharaoh, and the popular persuasion is already laying the groundwork: let's all come together and fight the demons coming from space. He neither lifted up his hand, nor held sword nor any instrument of war; but he sent out of his mouth as it had been a blast of fire, and it burnt them up every one, so that nothing was perceived but dust and smell of smoke.
precepts.point: And I saw the beast, and the kings of the earth, and their armies, gathered together to make war against him that sat on the horse, and against his army. There it is: gathered together, minds already persuaded. And the beast was taken, and with him the false prophet, and these both were cast alive into a lake of fire burning with brimstone.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
Revelation says the armies were gathered together to make war against him that sat on the horse and against his army. Ezra saw that same war. “there arose a wind from the sea”, and “that man waxed strong with the thousands of heaven: and when he turned his countenance to look, all the things trembled.” The man that came out of the sea is Christ, with the thousands of heaven, the armies that follow him.

And “whensoever the voice went out of his mouth, all they burned that heard his voice, like as the earth faileth when it feeleth the fire.” He speaks the laws out of his mouth, and the people just disintegrate, because they are guilty of that law. That is the sharp sword out of his mouth in Revelation, the laws of God.

Then “there was gathered together a multitude of men, out of number, from the four winds of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea”. They will have one consent, because the Most High is going to harden them like he did Pharaoh. And the popular persuasion is already laying the groundwork: let's all come together and fight the demons coming from space.

After this, “all they which were gathered together to subdue him were sore afraid, and yet durst fight.” Scared to death, but the Most High moves them. As Romans 9 shows, he built them up, just like ancient Egypt: Babylon the Great, this white man, this Edomite, built up just to be destroyed, made to fight against him.

And “he neither lifted up his hand, nor held sword, nor any instrument of war”, but sent out of his mouth “a blast of fire”, “a flaming breath”, and “sparks and tempests”, and “burned them up every one, so that upon a sudden of an innumerable multitude nothing was to be perceived, but only dust and smell of smoke.” Ashes to ashes, and dust to dust.

precepts.text: Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints. Those armies in heaven following him are the saints in the white robes, the ones that loved not their lives unto the death and received the immortal body. He is coming to execute judgment upon all, and to convince all that are ungodly of all their ungodly deeds, and of all their hard speeches which ungodly sinners have spoken against him.
precepts.point: I saw the beast, and the kings of the earth, and their armies, gathered together to make war against him that sat on the horse, and against his army. The kingdoms ruling the earth today really believe they can fight against Christ and the 144,000. And the beast was taken, and with him the false prophet, and these both were cast alive into a lake of fire: that is eternal damnation, not regular death. And the remnant were slain with the sword of him that sat upon the horse, which sword proceeded out of his mouth.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
“He that sat upon him was called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he doth judge and make war.” His vesture is “dipped in blood” because the Lord will be warring; enough nations are going to be slaughtered. “And the armies which were in heaven followed him upon white horses, clothed in fine linen, white and clean.” When Christ comes back, he is coming back with armies. You think he is coming back to kiss and shake hands? No. He is coming back for war, for deliverance, for vengeance.

So who are those armies that follow him? Jude answers: “And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints”. That is the armies: the saints in the white robes, the 144,000. Christ is coming back with his top Gs: the brothers that loved not their lives unto the death, that received their immortal body, clothed in fine linen, white and clean. They are coming back with the Lord for vengeance.

“To execute judgment upon all, and to convince all that are ungodly among them of all their ungodly deeds which they have ungodly committed, and of all their hard speeches which ungodly sinners have spoken against him.” All the hard speeches they have spoken against the Lord: the Lord is coming for vengeance.

Then “out of his mouth goeth a sharp sword, that with it he should smite the nations”. He is not using a literal weapon; he is using his words, and he is not coming to save the nations but to destroy them. The beast, America and Europe, and the kings of the earth will really believe they can gather their armies and fight against him and against his army of saints.

precepts.text: He hath on his vesture and on his thigh a name written, King of kings and Lord of lords. The King you will see in his beauty is Christ.
precepts.point: Jeremiah 46:27: fear not, O my servant Jacob, because Jacob's trouble and Armageddon are coming; I will save thee from afar off, this far-off land, and thy seed from the land of their captivity, and Jacob shall return and be in rest and at ease, and none shall make him afraid.

note.label: Hope Amid Destruction

precepts.why:
“And he hath on his vesture and on his thigh a name written, KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS.” When Isaiah 33:17 says “Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty”, it is talking about Christ. He is the King of kings; he is the Lord of lords.

Isaiah 33 asks who shall dwell with the devouring fire, who shall dwell with everlasting burnings before the Lord, and answers: he that walketh righteously and speaketh uprightly, speaking what the Bible says and living what it says; he that despiseth the gain of oppressions, the oppression you see as soon as you walk out these doors, which our brothers and sisters in the church make like they don't see; he that shaketh his hands from holding of bribes; he that stoppeth his ears from hearing of blood and shutteth his eyes from seeing evil. That one shall dwell on high.

And that one shall see the King. We want to see the Lord for ourselves, and the King we shall see in his beauty is Christ, with his name written on his vesture and on his thigh.

precepts.text: The Revelation of Jesus Christ. This proves who chapter 19 is describing.
precepts.point: He was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood, and his name is called the Word of God. Christ is about righteous destruction, as Isaiah 63 shows. When he comes back he is not meeting them as a man.

note.label: Wars Are Here: Seek Good Not Evil

precepts.why:
“His eyes were as a flame of fire, and on his head were many crowns; and he had a name written, that no man knew, but he himself.” No man knew it but he himself, so what are you tripping about, YHWH, Yahawashi, Jesus Christ? We are English speakers; we learned Jesus Christ. Call him what you call him, but we have to keep the commandments.

“And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God.” Why is his vesture dipped in blood? Because Christ is about righteous destruction; you read that in Isaiah 63. The Lord is a man of war. We serve a terrible God, and a merciful one, and he is going to use these nations to create a final battle.

How do we know this is Jesus? Revelation 1:1: “The Revelation of Jesus Christ”. The whole book is the revelation of who? Jesus Christ. So the rider of Revelation 19, with eyes as a flame of fire, is Jesus Christ, and when he comes back he is not going to meet them as a man.

That is our hope: to see it and be part of it, the kingdom where all the wrongs done to us get turned upside down and right is instilled in the earth. Not a pie-in-the-sky fairy tale from modern-day Christianity, but Christ coming back to make war.

precepts.text: His head and his hairs were white like wool, his eyes as a flame of fire, and his feet like unto fine brass as if they burned in a furnace. Jesus Christ was a black man; the Bible, archaeology, and history all say it, and everyone knows it except dumb Americans, and I was one. Christ is coming back to make war.
precepts.point: He was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood, and his name is called the Word of God. Christ is about righteous destruction, as Isaiah 63 shows. When he comes back he is not meeting them as a man.

note.label: Wars Are Here: Seek Good Not Evil

precepts.why:
The same Christ of Revelation 19, whose “eyes were as a flame of fire”, is described in chapter 1: “His head and his hairs were white like wool, as white as snow; and his eyes were as a flame of fire; And his feet like unto fine brass, as if they burned in a furnace”.

Why his feet like fine brass, as if burned in a furnace? Because you cannot deny it anymore: Jesus Christ was a black man. The Bible says it first and foremost, and there is archaeological proof and historical evidence besides. Everyone knows it except the dumb Americans here in this country, and I say that because I was a dumb American; we were all dumb at one point. A lot of Eastern Europeans know Jesus was black. Vladimir Putin knows Jesus was black.

So this is who is coming: the black Christ whose eyes are like a flame of fire, his vesture dipped in blood. Jesus Christ is coming back to make war. Understand that now, as the wars are here and God is orchestrating every one of them from the beginning.

precepts.text: His name is called The Word of God; the name of the Most High is his word.
precepts.point: Solomon's prayer is the humble spirit: give me neither poverty nor riches, feed me with food convenient for me. Full riches make a man deny the Most High and forget the congregation and the work, and money has pulled people out of this walk; poverty drives a man to steal. The chief things for life are simple, water, bread, clothing, and an house to cover shame, and the Most High blessed Solomon with riches because riches were not his god.

note.label: Deuteronomy 5: The Ten Commandments Reiterated

precepts.why:
“And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God.” The name of the Most High is his word.

That is what it means to take his name in vain. His name is called The Word of God, and the word of God is the book of the commandments; so to profane the commandments, stealing, lying, bearing false witness, committing adultery, is to profane the name. It was never about saying oh my god.

precepts.text: In righteousness He doth judge and make war, for justice and judgment are His throne.
precepts.point: Blessed is the people that know the joyful sound; they shall walk in the light of His countenance. We are going to walk in the laws and be before the Lord blameless like Abraham and our forefathers were.

note.label: Psalm 89: The Covenant Made with David

precepts.why:
“Justice and judgment are the habitation of thy throne: mercy and truth shall go before thy face.” That is the gospel, and John saw the one who sits on that throne come: “And I saw heaven opened, and behold a white horse; and he that sat upon him was called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he doth judge and make war.”

In righteousness he doth judge and make war, for justice and judgment are his throne. It is a great thing to have a just God who has the final authority, called Faithful and True.

We go through things, but this should build up your faith. It is why it is so important for things to be done decent and in order, the order that God established, because the one coming judges in righteousness.

precepts.text: The testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy; He comes in the volume of the book.
precepts.point: If each of us took a strong look at ourselves, we are more wise than before we came into the knowledge of the truth, because we should be growing in understanding as we continue to apply the commandments. The scriptures are spiritual; the law is spiritual.

note.label: Psalm 93: The Lord Reigneth and His Testimonies Are Sure

precepts.why:
His testimonies are very sure. John was told what the testimony is: “I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren that have the testimony of Jesus: worship God: for the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy.”

The testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy. He comes in the volume of the book; the sure testimonies of Psalm 93 are the prophecies that speak of Christ. The angel would not be worshipped but said worship God, because the testimony belongs to him.

As we apply the commandments and grow in understanding, we see that the scriptures are spiritual and the law is spiritual, and the sure testimony throughout is Christ.

precepts.text: He was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God.
precepts.point: The Word is Christ, and he was there in the beginning. The Word was with God, and the Word was of God: his wisdom and his power, which is why the same sentence can say both.

note.label: John 1: The Word, the Witness of John, and the King of Israel

precepts.why:
“In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” The Word is Christ, and he was there in the beginning. Revelation names him: “His eyes were as a flame of fire, and on his head were many crowns; and he had a name written, that no man knew, but he himself. And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God.”

The one clothed with a vesture dipped in blood is Christ, and his name is called The Word of God. So the Word that was with God in the beginning, “The same was in the beginning with God”, is Christ.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 3 A Message to The 7 Churches

precepts.why:
And they shall walk with me in white; this explains the walking in white. “And to her was granted that she should be arrayed in fine linen, clean and white: for the fine linen is the righteousness of saints.” See that: the fine linen is the righteousness of saints. So that is what that white represents, the righteousness of the saints. So we are not to have our garments defiled; that is what he is talking about, our spiritual clothing.

For they are worthy: you had a few brothers and sisters there that Christ said are worthy to walk with him in righteousness, but the rest of you. He doesn't mention any names, so the whole church needs to do self-examination: is this me?

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 3 A Message to The 7 Churches

precepts.why:
I will write upon him my new name: so Christ has a new name. For all you Yeshua or Yahawashi people: if you want to say it, that is fine, but don't make it a doctrine where you say if you don't say it you can't be saved. Don't do that. I made the mistake, and you all circulate the videos from '94 or '95: oh look, he taught the name. I made a mistake saying if you don't say it the way I said it you are going to be put to death, and that was wrong.

“His eyes were as a flame of fire, and on his head were many crowns; and he had a name written, that no man knew, but he himself.” See, Israelites don't believe that. They say no, we know the name; you all don't know it but we know. It says that no man knew but he himself, but the Negroes in New York know it? Are you kidding me? The Negroes in Harlem know it? Stop it.
